content.user_title: Plan projects with parallel research agents
content.value_statement: Early project decisions often rely on incomplete technical and market information. This skill coordinates specialist research agents and combines their evidence into one planning report.
actual_capabilities: Dispatches technology, architecture, and market research agents in parallel.
Adds UX trend research when the --deep option is selected.
Uses existing project documentation to prepare a research brief.
Checks agent outputs for sources, relevance, format, and contradictions.
Combines findings into ranked technology and architecture recommendations.
Creates a dated Markdown research report or prints the result to the terminal.
limitations: Research quality depends on the sources available to the agents.
It provides recommendations, not implementation or code changes.
Context7 research runs only when that MCP tool is installed.
It does not replace security, legal, or domain-expert review.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a new product stack
use_cases.description: Compare frameworks, databases, and libraries before committing to a greenfield product.

use_cases.title: Prepare an architecture decision
use_cases.description: Collect evidence about architecture patterns and trade-offs for an existing product.

use_cases.title: Study a competitive market
use_cases.description: Combine product comparisons with technical and UX research for a product discovery brief.

prompt_templates.title: Quick project research
prompt_templates.prompt: /team-research Build a scheduling app for small clinics --quick
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with core technology, architecture, and market research.

prompt_templates.title: Full product discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: /team-research Research a subscription analytics platform for independent creators
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a standard cross-functional research report.

prompt_templates.title: Deep UX and market study
prompt_templates.prompt: /team-research Design an offline-first inventory app for field technicians --deep
prompt_templates.scenario: Include UX trend research with technical and market findings.

prompt_templates.title: Research without a file
prompt_templates.prompt: /team-research Compare options for a B2B document approval service --deep --stdout
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the complete research result in the terminal before saving it.

output_examples.input: Research an offline-first inventory application for field technicians.
output: A technology comparison covering local databases and encryption libraries.
An architecture recommendation for synchronization and offline conflict handling.
A market and UX summary with sources, risks, and ranked alternatives.

output_examples.input: Run quick research for a clinic scheduling application.
output_examples.output: A concise report with technology, architecture, and competitor findings, followed by a recommended first-choice stack.

best_practices: Provide the target users, important constraints, and technologies to avoid.
Use --deep when UX trends could change the product direction.
Review cited sources and validate recommendations before making commitments.
anti_patterns: Do not treat uncited research as a final decision.
Do not include credentials, private customer data, or API keys in the project brief.
Do not use the report as a substitute for security, legal, or compliance review.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a dated Markdown research report or a terminal summary with cross-checked recommendations.

faq.question: What is included in quick mode?
faq.answer: Quick mode uses technology, architecture, and market research agents.

faq.question: What does deep mode add?
faq.answer: Deep mode adds a UX research agent to the standard research workflow.

faq.question: Does the skill modify application code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for research and report generation only.

faq.question: Is Context7 required?
faq.answer: No. Context7 is used only when installed, and the skill can otherwise rely on web research.

faq.question: Can I avoid creating a report file?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the --stdout option to show the research result in the terminal.
